reviews.text: On paper, that description undoubtedly seems ridiculous. But remember -- what The 13th Warrior does best is make the ridiculous seem (for lack of a better word) "cool."
reviews.author: Chuck Klosterman

reviews.text: All in all it proved to be a cinematic outing that was definitely unlucky for some.
reviews.author: Alistair Lawrence

reviews.text: Akira Kurosawa's brilliant samurai movies -- especially 1957's Throne of Blood -- are a visual influence. But the script lacks the dignity that infuses Kurosawa's equally blood-thirsty characters.
reviews.author: Paul Tatara

reviews.text: Exciting battle sequences, intriguing period costumes, fascinating cinematography, and stirring background music contribute to the epic nature of 'The 13th Warrior.'
reviews.author: Betty Jo Tucker

reviews.text: "The 13th Warrior" is a brazen attempt to brand Antonio Banderas as an A-lister with a C-grade script. Failure attends.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Jerry Goldsmith's rousing score exhibits more personality than any of the actors--or anything else in the film, for that matter.
reviews.author: Michael Dequina

reviews.text: Michael Crichton's story is underdeveloped and narrow in range, resulting in a tale more curious for its odd confluence of elements than for their edifying deployment.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: Mr. Crichton may have found the perfect venue for his particular brand of character underdevelopment.
reviews.author: Joe Lozito

reviews.text: Shelved for over a year and probably heavily edited, it's better than it could have been.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: At its best, this achieves the beauty and grandeur of a Kurosawa epic -- at its worst, however, it feels like a Python remake of The Vikings.
reviews.author: Geoff Andrew

reviews.text: If you're in the mood to watch heads, arms and other appendages getting chopped off, this movie is for you.
reviews.author: Chris Gore

reviews.text: The film is fascinating to watch, but I can hardly say what it's about, other than people killing each other.
reviews.author: Jeff Millar

reviews.text: It harks back to the late 1950s when people actually made movies about Vikings and other seafaring heroes named Sinbad and Jason.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Westhoff

reviews.text: An entertaining and serviceable adaptation. Dennis Storhoi delivers an awesome performance. Weak aspects of story made up for by great action.
reviews.author: Brian Mckay

reviews.text: Although the subject matter is not too pleasant and the gore is turned up to 11, Crichton's film is an excellent Nordic war story.
reviews.author: John R. McEwen

reviews.text: The film is based on Eaters of the Dead, possibly the worst novel Michael Crichton has ever written, and this film isn't even a passable adaptation.
reviews.author: Jeff Vice

reviews.text: For fans of the genre, it's an inexorably primal exercise almost like cinematic steroids: qualitatively lacking, if not harmful, yet superficially irresistible.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: A sensao que fica, ao final da projeo,  a de que vimos um filme vazio - e sobre o personagem errado. E o que  pior: no qual nada acontece.
reviews.author: Pablo Villaça

reviews.text: A big cathartic blast.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: The screenplay effectively communicates the cross-cultural tensions between the Arabs, the Vikings, and the pagan Wendols.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: everything is first rate except the characters and the story
reviews.author: Blake French

reviews.text: Mediocrity should never be encouraged.
reviews.author: Andrew Howe

reviews.text: Stay home and watch the WWF. The only difference is; they don't fight with swords
reviews.author: Kamal  'The Diva' Larsuel

reviews.text: The movie itself is unfulfilling. It just hangs there, like the aftertaste of stale beer.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Actually a well-marbled, albeit derivative, slab of action-movie man meat.
reviews.author: Gary Dauphin

reviews.text: A widescreen epic adventure so beautifully designed and performed that it doesn't have to make a bit of sense.
reviews.author: Steven Boone

reviews.text: The 13th Warrior reeks so badly of melodrama and poor acting that it carries a worst scent than a canine's least appetizing residue.
reviews.author: Mac Verstandig

reviews.text: Stupefyingly horrendous.
reviews.author: Dustin Putman

reviews.text: The 13th Warrior is simply without thrills and excitement.
reviews.author: Christopher Null

reviews.text: Character development? Nil. Plot twists? Zip. Emotional involvement with anyone in the movie? Nada.
reviews.author: Lawrence Toppman

reviews.text: An abbreviated and shallow epic that comes off like an over-produced and dead-serious episode of the campy cult TV show Xena: Warrior Princess.
reviews.author: Rob Blackwelder

reviews.text: The whole mess is often too busy to get down to business.
reviews.author: Scott Renshaw

reviews.text: It falls short where it counts: in the final confrontation.
reviews.author: Bob Graham

reviews.text: The 13th Warrior is a kick in the 10th century.
Loaded with potential, it's puzzlingly overblown and distant, as if its huge budget were an albatross around its neck.
reviews.author: Michael Wilmington

reviews.text: Michael Crichton is quite a character; his films could use a little.
reviews.author: Eugene Novikov

reviews.text: A Strong B+
reviews.author: Ross Anthony

reviews.text: Annoying and dull.
reviews.author: Ian Mantgani

reviews.text: Stilted dialogue, ridiculous storyline and spurting arteries combine for a very ugly filmgoing experience.
reviews.author: Jeanne Aufmuth

reviews.text: [Banderas is] playing an Arab character with a Spanish dialect, interacting with English-speaking Norsemen who look and act like a biker gang.
reviews.author: Gary Brown

reviews.text: A dull, dark, beautifully photographed but nonsensical sword - and - sorcery wannabe epic.
reviews.author: Philip Booth

reviews.text: The actual story is really nothing more than a continuous and extremely gory battle scene, filled with missing heads, hacked-off limbs, and pools of blood.
reviews.author: Jim Chastain

reviews.text: This stinker barks. It has been fermenting for a couple of years as the creative minds behind it continued to cut, recut then cut again, trying to make steak out of ground beef.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: The cheese flows fast and furious from the screen.
reviews.author: Gabriel Shanks

reviews.text: Much blood. Much mud. Not enough camp.
reviews.author: Cynthia Fuchs

reviews.text: The 13th Warrior seems like a made-for-TV warrior movie without enough money to get really epic.
reviews.author: Desson Thomson

reviews.text: Banderas creates a sympathetic hero, the script is remarkably free of '90-isms, the Viking characters are engaging, and The 13th Warrior offers some of the rousing retro pleasures of a good '50s cavalry - and - Indians B-movie.
reviews.author: William Arnold

reviews.text: . Seeing "The 13th Warrior" is like wishing for light at the end of a long dark tunnel, when we both know nothing is really there.
reviews.author: David Keyes

reviews.text: The 13th Warrior contains the raw materials of an offbeat adventure, but fails to achieve the rousing mood or narrative glory of a grand epic.
reviews.author: Jack Garner

reviews.text: You're either caught between nothing happening for long scenes of beautiful vista watching, or things happen and are never followed up on.
reviews.author: Widgett Walls

reviews.text: It neither follows a trend nor sets one.
reviews.author: Duane Dudek

reviews.text: Ludicrously bad!
reviews.author: Steve Rhodes

reviews.text: The film falls short of its goal to find a distinct personality and never attains the suspension of belief required of genre films like Conan or 7th Voyage of Sinbad.
reviews.author: Tony Toscano

reviews.text: With a budget said to be more than $100 million, it displays a lot of cash on the screen, but little thought.
reviews.author: Roger Ebert

reviews.text: The film feels as if it had a bad run through the editing room.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Director John McTiernan did this long before The Hunt for Red October and he would be wise to leave it off his resume.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: As far as medieval action adventure epics are concerned, they don't come more proficient than this one.
reviews.author: Urban Cinefile Critics

reviews.text: The most unexpectedly audacious, exhilarating, and wildly creative adventure thriller I have seen in ages!
reviews.author: Lisa Schwarzbaum

reviews.text: The best, most enthralling adventure movie I've seen in a good while.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Never really wowed me while I was watching it, but I grew more impressed with it afterwards.
reviews.author: Marty Mapes

reviews.text: Los que busquen profundidad en la historia se van a sentir algo decepcionados
reviews.author: Jorge Avila Andrade

reviews.text: A mud-stained, blood-soaked and completely useless movie.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Banderas puts in a decent turn, but it's Norwegian newcomer Dennis Storhoi who steals the show; his charming, effortless performance shows both the perils and pleasures of being a Viking.
reviews.author: Tor Thorsen

reviews.text: See it if you like films which start off slow, have plenty of scenes in the dark, a few good battle sequences and incomprehensible men talking bunk.
reviews.author: JoBlo

reviews.text: Funny, although it doesn't mean to be.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: Here was a film with a scope far beyond the reaches of a mediocre director like Crichton.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: The acting is quite good, with Banderas showing once again the charm and athletic ability he brought to The Mask of Zorro.
reviews.author: David Forsmark

reviews.text: Amounts to little more than a jumble of fire, horses and gory battle scenes. Amidst the constant flow of blood and mud and rain, you kind of feel dirty having just sat through it.
reviews.author: Thom Bennett

reviews.text: "Warrior" is simply a mess. It does, however, offer the sight of Antonio Banderas (in eyeliner, no less) struggling to portray an Arab soldier, which must be one of the most curious casting choices since Demi Moore played a Puritan.
reviews.author: James Sanford

reviews.text: With the possible exception of the action sequences and the very occasionally imaginative set design, it's awful.
reviews.author: Peter Brunette

reviews.text: It's not a good sign when what the filmmakers seemingly intended to be a straightforward action film leaves the viewers saying, 'Huh?'
reviews.author: Shay Casey

reviews.text: If the juiciest bouts of professional wrestling on television leave you feeling unfulfilled and pining for the primal howls of fight - to - the - death combat, The 13th Warrior just might be the answer to your prayers.
reviews.author: Stephen Holden

reviews.text: An exhilarating 100 minutes!
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Murky, all - but - impossible to follow battle sequences.
reviews.author: Maitland McDonagh

reviews.text: Let's face it. Kull: The Conqueror, as dumb and as hokey as it gets, was a lot more fun.
reviews.author: G. Allen Johnson

reviews.text: There's intense action and terrific violence for much of this film.
reviews.author: Brian Webster

reviews.text: As movies about Norsemen go, it's not as witty as The Vikings with Kirk Douglas, but it holds your attention through sheer cinematic power.
reviews.author: Jonathan Foreman

reviews.text: The 13th Warrior indulges in enough grubby histrionics and costume-adventure clichs to give you fifth-grade flashbacks.
reviews.author: Michael Atkinson

reviews.text: Often quite entertaining, if not for the Emma crowd.
reviews.author: David Elliott

reviews.text: The actors keep the film from becoming too stupid
reviews.author: Carlo Cavagna

synopsis: A Muslim ambassador exiled from his homeland, Ahmad ibn Fadlan (Antonio Banderas) finds himself in the company of Vikings. While the behavior of the Norsemen initially offends ibn Fadlan, the more cultured outsider grows to respect the tough, if uncouth, warriors. During their travels together, ibn Fadlan and the Vikings get word of an evil presence closing in, and they must fight the frightening and formidable force, which was previously thought to exist only in legend.
